most_likely_explanation: A ~1.1 h, ~1600 ppm (box; ~2000 ppm true after cadence smearing) periodic dimming at 2.3770144 d located on the target's own pixel in all 17 quarters and all four CCD channels, with no eclipse-like signature from either bright neighbour (host KIC 9520088 shows -6 +- 12 ppm at the ephemeris; its pixels show -11 ppm median), no catalogued object sharing the ephemeris, clean inverted null, consistent odd/even depth and timing, and constant depth across seasons. Consistent with a ~3 Re object transiting the K dwarf at b ~ 0.85. Two open items remain: a marginal (2.2-2.8 sigma, estimator-dependent) brightening at phase 0.5 that no planet produces and that makes the signal a formal stage-2 FAIL under the post-hoc v1.5 rule (c) which was added because of this very star; and the generic unresolved-blend risk (background EB fainter than Gaia's G~21 limit inside the 4-arcsec pixel, or a bound companion EB) which Kepler pixels cannot test.
surviving_strengths: Independent per-pixel test on the 17 cached TPFs of KIC 9520088: deficit in the target's pixel in every quarter (per-quarter SNR 3.2-10.7, combined 1.02 +- 0.04 e/s, 24.5 sigma, ~1400 ppm of that pixel's flux), quantitatively matching 1537 e/s x 1570 ppm x psffrac 0.61 = 1.5 e/s in-stamp; the five host-dominated pixels show -0.33 +- 0.51 e/s (median -11 ppm), excluding a blend from the G 14.8 host by a factor > 50

KBONUS PSF light curves of the neighbours at the ephemeris: KIC 9520088 (G 14.8, 10 arcsec) -6 +- 12 ppm; KIC 9520089 (G 13.9, 19 arcsec) -190 +- 210 ppm; neither can feed 1500 ppm into a crowdsap-0.98 aperture

The only other Gaia source within 15 arcsec is G 20.88 at 3.5 arcsec (0.87 px); in the 13 quarters where it occupies a different pixel from the target the deficit ratio is 1.01 : 0.24 e/s in favour of the target pixel (pipeline chi2 fits agree, summed dchi2 ~ 220); Gaia DR3 TAP cone confirms the neighbour list is complete and the target has RUWE 1.15, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, non_single_star 0

No KOI, DR25 TCE, Kepler EB or confirmed planet within 3 arcmin; field-wide period/harmonic match (1:1, 1:2, 2:1, 1:3, 3:1) finds nothing within 1e-5 fractional except Kepler-113 c at 2:1 (748 ppm, 4.8 deg away, epoch phase 0.48, no odd/even alternation): not a contaminant; TPF host and KIC 9520089 have no KOI/TCE/EB entry

Same depth on four different channels (seasons: 1500 +- 144, 1518 +- 97, 1552 +- 132, 1789 +- 126 ppm; channels 62/46/22/38), constant per year (chi2 4.7/3), no gap-distance dependence; 2.377 d is not a momentum-dump, cadence or quarter alias

Odd/even 1.13 sigma with odd and even transit centres agreeing to 1.4 min (no e cos w signature of a period-doubled EB); no secondary eclipse (dip >= ~120 ppm at phase 0.5 excluded at 2 sigma); SAP/PSF depth ratio 0.94 vs 0.98 expected (no brighter contaminant in the SAP aperture)
No variability at P or its harmonics (LS power at P, P/2, 2P < 5e-5 vs 1e-3 at the unrelated 0.286 d peak); inverted-flux null flat (re-derivation SDE 7.5 vs 108)

The pipeline's per-event chi2 inflation (912/467) and the low third time-quartile depth (1091 ppm weighted vs 1708 ppm median) are both due to one event (n=342, BKJD 945.09, Q10) with isolated +6000-8000 ppm single-cadence spikes and an under-estimated error; removing it gives ~1.5, matching the positive controls
Not in Bienias & Szabo 2025 (7 KICs checked), not a TOI/CTOI within 5 arcmin, no SIMBAD EB/variable within 30 arcsec; KIC 9520080 was never a Kepler target
Duration 1.125-1.15 h is consistent with the K-dwarf host (a/Rs 9.5, T14(b=0) 1.99 h) at b ~ 0.85; implied Rp ~ 3.0 Re (box) to ~3.3 Re (smearing-corrected)

what_would_settle_it: Ground-based transit photometry at predicted times (~2000 ppm true depth, 1.1 h, G 17.5; 1-2 m class) to confirm the event on the target at sub-arcsec resolution and separate it from the G 20.9 star at 3.5 arcsec

TRICERATOPS (or equivalent) false-positive probability using the Gaia neighbour list and a contrast curve, to bound the G > 21 background-EB and bound-companion-EB scenarios that Kepler pixels cannot test
AO or speckle imaging of the target to bound companions inside 1 arcsec

An independent re-examination of the phase-0.5 brightening (second detrending family, PSF-vs-SAP at phase 0.5 per quarter); if real at ~200 ppm it is not a planet signature and the signal should be downgraded
